title: HR Analytics: Nirmaan Technologies
description: Nirmaan Technologies is a fictional 2,400-person Indian tech and services company with eight departments across Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi. The dataset links employees to appraisal-cycle salary changes, half-yearly performance reviews and exits during 2023-2024. Use it to analyse attrition drivers, pay equity, hike policy and workforce planning.

tables.name: departments
tables.description: Eight departments with budget and head.

tables.name: employees
tables.description: One row per employee ever employed 2023-2024 (12 duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: employee_id
columns.description: Employee identifier (duplicated for the duplicate rows)

columns.name: job_level
columns.description: Junior, Mid, Senior, Lead or Manager

columns.name: manager_id
columns.description: FK to employees.employee_id (NULL for top managers)

columns.name: employment_status
columns.description: Active or Exited (matches the attrition table)

tables.name: salaries
tables.description: Salary history: opening/joining CTC and April appraisal revisions.

columns.name: annual_ctc
columns.description: Annual cost-to-company in INR (5 rows are 100x outliers)

columns.name: hike_pct
columns.description: Percentage hike versus the previous CTC (NULL for opening/joining rows)

columns.name: change_reason
columns.description: Opening balance, Joining, Annual Appraisal or Promotion

tables.name: attrition
tables.description: One row per employee who left in 2023-2024.

columns.name: exit_type
columns.description: Resignation, Termination, Retirement or End of Contract

tables.name: performance_reviews
tables.description: Half-yearly reviews 2023-H1 to 2024-H1 (10 duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: avg_monthly_overtime_hours
columns.description: Average monthly overtime hours in the period

qualityIssues: employees: 12 exact duplicate rows (same employee_id twice), so employee_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint; performance_reviews: 10 exact duplicate rows.
employees.gender: ~6% of rows use 'M'/'F' instead of 'Male'/'Female'.
employees.city: ~9% have inconsistent casing/whitespace ('pune', ' Pune'), ~2% NULL; employees.email ~4% NULL.
employees.manager_id is NULL for top-level managers (~5% of employees).
salaries.annual_ctc: 5 rows are 100x outliers (e.g. 120,000,000 instead of 1,200,000).
salaries.hike_pct is NULL for opening-balance and joining rows (about 45% of salary rows).
attrition.exit_interview_score is NULL for ~30% of exits.
CSV only - employees.hire_date and employees.date_of_birth: ~20% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY.
CSV only - salaries.annual_ctc: ~30% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping (e.g. '₹12,50,000').
CSV only - performance_reviews.review_date: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY.

signals: [Instructor note] Attrition is driven by (a) low manager ratings, (b) high average overtime (> ~10 h/month), and (c) low appraisal hikes (< ~4%); employees with all three leave at several times the base rate.
[Instructor note] Customer Support, Sales and Operations have the highest attrition; Finance and HR the lowest; employees with < 2 years tenure leave more.
[Instructor note] Exits spike in April-June (post-appraisal) and Nov-Jan (post-bonus).
[Instructor note] Hike % tracks performance (about +3 points per rating step) while Sales gets ~1 point lower hikes.
[Instructor note] Customer Support has the lowest CTC but the highest overtime; Engineering and Product pay ~25-30% more than average.
[Instructor note] Overtime-heavy exits cite 'Work-life balance / overtime' far more often in exit_reason.
[Instructor note] 5 salary outliers (100x) distort average CTC unless excluded.
